newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian Airlines sees profits up.
newsitem.headline: Austrian Airlines sees profits up.

text.p: Austrian flag carrier Austrian Airlines said on Friday it was poised to return to lasting profitability although prices would remain under pressure over the next few years.
"We can expect continuing growth over the next years. We are striving to increase productivity and to show steady profits," chief executive Herbert Bammer told an investors' conference.
The five-year plan foresaw a continuous increase in sales to 16.8 billion schillings, and a rise in pre-tax profit to between 800 to 900 billion schillings.
In 1995, the airline reported group sales of 11.7 billion schillings and a pre-tax profit of 65.9 million schillings.

Bammer reiterated earlier statements that the airline expected its 1996 profits to be around the previous year's levels. Rising fuel costs over the year had resulted in extra cost burden of about 100 million schillings, he said.
Bammer added that 1997 should see a strong rise in earnings, helped by continuing cost savings measures. "The goal for 1997 is a pretax profit of 300 million," he said.

Austrian Airlines said it aimed to increase its passenger load factor to 62 percent from 60 percent currently. "Every one percent more brings 160 million schillings in earnings," finance chief Fritz Otti said.
Despite an expected average growth of six percent in world air traffic over the next years, prices would remain under pressure, forcing the airline to keep costs under strict control, Bammer said.

The chief executive said the recently strengthened alliance with Swissair, Delta Airlines and Sabena should also bring in extra revenue. The companies agreed in December to introduce joint operations across the North Atlantic from February.
